NKJV.1: Then God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the animals that were with him in the ark. And God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
NKJV.2: The fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were also stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
NKJV.3: And the waters receded continually from the earth. At the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters decreased.
NKJV.4: Then the ark rested in the seventh month, the seventeenth day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.
NKJV.5: And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
NKJV.6: So it came to pass, at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
NKJV.7: Then he sent out a raven, which kept going to and fro until the waters had dried up from the earth.
NKJV.8: He also sent out from himself a dove, to see if the waters had receded from the face of the ground.
NKJV.9: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned into the ark to him, for the waters were on the face of the whole earth. So he put out his hand and took her, and drew her into the ark to himself.
NKJV.10: And he waited yet another seven days, and again he sent the dove out from the ark.
NKJV.11: Then the dove came to him in the evening, and behold, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her mouth; and Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
NKJV.12: So he waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove, which did not return again to him anymore.
NKJV.13: And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, that the waters were dried up from the earth; and Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and indeed the surface of the ground was dry.
NKJV.14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dried.
NKJV.15: Then God spoke to Noah, saying,
NKJV.16: “Go out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.
NKJV.17: Bring out with you every living thing of all flesh that is with you: birds and cattle and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, so that they may abound on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
NKJV.18: So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him.
NKJV.19: Every animal, every creeping thing, every bird, and whatever creeps on the earth, according to their families, went out of the ark.
NKJV.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
NKJV.21: And the LORD smelled a soothing aroma. Then the LORD said in His heart, “I will never again curse the ground for man’s sake, although the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; nor will I again destroy every living thing as I have done.
NKJV.22: “While the earth remains, Seedtime and harvest, Cold and heat, Winter and summer, And day and night Shall not cease.”

ESV.1: But God remembered Noah and all the beasts and all the livestock that were with him in the ark. And God made a wind blow over the earth, and the waters subsided.
ESV.2: The fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, the rain from the heavens was restrained,
ESV.3: and the waters receded from the earth continually. At the end of 150 days the waters had abated,
ESV.4: and in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
ESV.5: And the waters continued to abate until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
ESV.6: At the end of forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made
ESV.7: and sent forth a raven. It went to and fro until the waters were dried up from the earth.
ESV.8: Then he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters had subsided from the face of the ground.
ESV.9: But the dove found no place to set her foot, and she returned to him to the ark, for the waters were still on the face of the whole earth. So he put out his hand and took her and brought her into the ark with him.
ESV.10: He waited another seven days, and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark.
ESV.11: And the dove came back to him in the evening, and behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth.
ESV.12: Then he waited another seven days and sent forth the dove, and she did not return to him anymore.
ESV.13: In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried from off the earth. And Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.
ESV.14: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth had dried out.
ESV.16: “Go out from the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons' wives with you.
ESV.17: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh — birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth — that they may swarm on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
ESV.18: So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
ESV.19: Every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird, everything that moves on the earth, went out by families from the ark.
ESV.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD and took some of every clean animal and some of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
ESV.21: And when the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, the LORD said in his heart, “I will never again curse  the ground because of man, for the intention of man's heart is evil from his youth. Neither will I ever again strike down every living creature as I have done.
ESV.22: While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease.”

NASB.1: But God remembered Noah and all the beasts and all the cattle that were with him in the ark; and God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the water subsided.
NASB.2: Also the fountains of the deep and the floodgates of the sky were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained;
NASB.3: and the water receded steadily from the earth, and at the end of one hundred and fifty days the water decreased.
NASB.4: In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.
NASB.5: The water decreased steadily until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains became visible.
NASB.6: Then it came about at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made;
NASB.7: and he sent out a raven, and it flew here and there until the water was dried up from the earth.
NASB.8: Then he sent out a dove from him, to see if the water was abated from the face of the land;
NASB.9: but the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, so she returned to him into the ark, for the water was on the surface of all the earth. Then he put out his hand and took her, and brought her into the ark to himself.
NASB.10: So he waited yet another seven days; and again he sent out the dove from the ark.
NASB.11: The dove came to him toward evening, and behold, in her beak was a freshly picked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the water was abated from the earth.
NASB.12: Then he waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; but she did not return to him again.
NASB.13: Now it came about in the six hundred and first year, in the first [month], on the first of the month, the water was dried up from the earth. Then Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dried up.
NASB.14: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
NASB.15: Then God spoke to Noah, saying,
NASB.16: 'Go out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives with you.
NASB.17: 'Bring out with you every living thing of all flesh that is with you, birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.'
NASB.18: So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
NASB.19: Every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird, everything that moves on the earth, went out by their families from the ark.
NASB.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
NASB.21: The LORD smelled the soothing aroma; and the LORD said to Himself, 'I will never again curse the ground on account of man, for the intent of man's heart is evil from his youth; and I will never again destroy every living thing, as I have done.
NASB.22: 'While the earth remains, Seedtime and harvest, And cold and heat, And summer and winter, And day and night Shall not cease.'

CSB17.1: God remembered Noah, <sup>ⓒ</sup> as well as all the wildlife and all the livestock that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind <sup>[1]</sup> to pass over the earth, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the water began to subside.
CSB17.2: The sources of the watery depths and the floodgates of the sky were closed, and the rain from the sky stopped. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.3: The water steadily receded from the earth, and by the end of 150 days the water had decreased significantly. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.4: The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.5: The water continued to recede until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were visible.
CSB17.6: After forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made,
CSB17.7: and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.
CSB17.8: Then he sent out a dove to see whether the water on the earth’s surface had gone down,
CSB17.9: but the dove found no resting place for its foot. It returned to him in the ark because water covered the surface of the whole earth. He reached out and brought it into the ark to himself.
CSB17.10: So Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove from the ark again.
CSB17.11: When the dove came to him at evening, there was a plucked olive leaf in its beak. So Noah knew that the water on the earth’s surface had gone down.
CSB17.12: After he had waited another seven days, he sent out the dove, but it did not return to him again.
CSB17.13: In the six hundred and first year, <sup>[2]</sup> in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water that had covered the earth was dried up. Then Noah removed the ark’s cover and saw that the surface of the ground was drying.
CSB17.14: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was dry.
CSB17.16: “Come out of the ark, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.
CSB17.17: Bring out all the living creatures <sup>[3]</sup> that are with you — birds, livestock, those that crawl on the earth — and they will spread over the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.18: So Noah, along with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, came out.
CSB17.19: All the animals, all the creatures that crawl, and all the flying creatures — everything that moves on the earth — came out of the ark by their families.
CSB17.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every kind of clean animal and every kind of clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
CSB17.21: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, <sup>ⓘ</sup> he said to himself, “I will never again curse the ground <sup>ⓙ</sup> because of human beings, even though the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth onward. <sup>ⓚ</sup> And I will never again strike down every living thing as I have done. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.22:
As long as the earth endures,
seedtime and harvest, cold and heat,
summer and winter, and day and night
will not cease.” ⓜ

WEB.1: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.
WEB.2: The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
WEB.3: The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the waters decreased.
WEB.4: The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s mountains.
WEB.5: The waters receded continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were visible.
WEB.6: At the end of forty days, Noah opened the window of the ship which he had made,
WEB.7: and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth, until the waters were dried up from the earth.
WEB.8: He himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground,
WEB.9: but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
WEB.10: He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
WEB.11: The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.
WEB.12: He waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him anymore.
WEB.13: In the six hundred first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the ground was dried.
WEB.14: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
WEB.16: “Go out of the ship, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.
WEB.17: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”
WEB.18: Noah went out, with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him.
WEB.19: Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatever moves on the earth, after their families, went out of the ship.
WEB.20: Noah built an altar to Yahweh, and took of every clean animal, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
WEB.21: Yahweh smelled the pleasant aroma. Yahweh said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.
WEB.22: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”

NLT.1: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and livestock with him in the boat. He sent a wind to blow across the earth, and the floodwaters began to recede.
NLT.2: The underground waters stopped flowing, and the torrential rains from the sky were stopped.
NLT.3: So the floodwaters gradually receded from the earth. After 150 days,
NLT.4: exactly five months from the time the flood began, the boat came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
NLT.5: Two and a half months later, as the waters continued to go down, other mountain peaks became visible.
NLT.6: After another forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the boat
NLT.7: and released a raven. The bird flew back and forth until the floodwaters on the earth had dried up.
NLT.8: He also released a dove to see if the water had receded and it could find dry ground.
NLT.9: But the dove could find no place to land because the water still covered the ground. So it returned to the boat, and Noah held out his hand and drew the dove back inside.
NLT.10: After waiting another seven days, Noah released the dove again.
NLT.11: This time the dove returned to him in the evening with a fresh olive leaf in its beak. Then Noah knew that the floodwaters were almost gone.
NLT.12: He waited another seven days and then released the dove again. This time it did not come back.
NLT.13: Noah was now 601 years old. On the first day of the new year, ten and a half months after the flood began, the floodwaters had almost dried up from the earth. Noah lifted back the covering of the boat and saw that the surface of the ground was drying.
NLT.14: Two more months went by, and at last the earth was dry!
NLT.16: “Leave the boat, all of you — you and your wife, and your sons and their wives.
NLT.17: Release all the animals — the birds, the livestock, and the small animals that scurry along the ground — so they can be fruitful and multiply throughout the earth.”
NLT.18: So Noah, his wife, and his sons and their wives left the boat.
NLT.19: And all of the large and small animals and birds came out of the boat, pair by pair.
NLT.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and there he sacrificed as burnt offerings the animals and birds that had been approved for that purpose.
NLT.21: And the LORD was pleased with the aroma of the sacrifice and said to himself, “I will never again curse the ground because of the human race, even though everything they think or imagine is bent toward evil from childhood. I will never again destroy all living things.
NLT.22: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night.”

AMP.1: And God remembered and thought kindly of Noah and every living thing and all the animals that were with him in the ark; and God made a wind blow over the land, and the waters receded.
AMP.2: Also the fountains of the deep [subterranean waters] and the windows of the heavens were closed, the [pouring] rain from the sky was restrained,
AMP.3: and the waters receded steadily from the earth. At the end of a hundred and fifty days the waters had diminished.
AMP.4: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month [five months after the rain began], the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat [in Turkey].
AMP.5: The waters continued to decrease until the tenth month; on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains were seen.
AMP.6: At the end of [another] forty days Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made;
AMP.7: and he sent out a raven, which flew here and there until the waters were dried up from the earth.
AMP.8: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the water level had fallen below the surface of the land.
AMP.9: But the dove found no place on which to rest the sole of her foot, and she returned to him to the ark, for the waters were [still] on the face of the entire earth. So he reached out his hand and took the dove, and brought her into the ark.
AMP.10: He waited another seven days and again sent the dove out from the ark.
AMP.11: The dove came back to him in the evening, and there, in her beak, was a fresh olive leaf. So Noah knew that the water level had subsided from the earth.
AMP.12: Then he waited another seven days and sent out the dove, but she did not return to him again.
AMP.13: Now in the six hundred and first year [of Noah's life], on the first day of the first month, the waters were drying up from the earth. Then Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and the surface of the ground was drying.
AMP.14: On the twenty-seventh day of the second month the land was [entirely] dry.
AMP.15: And God spoke to Noah, saying,
AMP.16: "Go out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and their wives with you.
AMP.17: Bring out with you every living thing from all flesh—birds and animals and every crawling thing that crawls on the earth—that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth."
AMP.18: So Noah went out, and his wife and his sons and their wives with him [after being in the ark one year and ten days].
AMP.19: Every animal, every crawling thing, every bird—and whatever moves on the land—went out by families (types, groupings) from the ark.
AMP.20: And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every [ceremonially] clean animal and of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
AMP.21: The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma [a soothing, satisfying scent] and the LORD said to Himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of man, for the intent (strong inclination, desire) of man's heart is wicked from his youth; and I will never again destroy every living thing, as I have done.
AMP.22:
"While the earth remains,
Seedtime and harvest,
Cold and heat,
Winter and summer,
And day and night
Shall not cease."

NRSVCE.1: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and all the domestic animals that were with him in the ark. And God made a wind blow over the earth, and the waters subsided;
NRSVCE.2: the fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, the rain from the heavens was restrained,
NRSVCE.3: and the waters gradually receded from the earth. At the end of one hundred fifty days the waters had abated;
NRSVCE.4: and in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
NRSVCE.5: The waters continued to abate until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
NRSVCE.6: At the end of forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made
NRSVCE.7: and sent out the raven; and it went to and fro until the waters were dried up from the earth.
NRSVCE.8: Then he sent out the dove from him, to see if the waters had subsided from the face of the ground;
NRSVCE.9: but the dove found no place to set its foot, and it returned to him to the ark, for the waters were still on the face of the whole earth. So he put out his hand and took it and brought it into the ark with him.
NRSVCE.10: He waited another seven days, and again he sent out the dove from the ark;
NRSVCE.11: and the dove came back to him in the evening, and there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf; so Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth.
NRSVCE.12: Then he waited another seven days, and sent out the dove; and it did not return to him any more.
NRSVCE.13: In the six hundred first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth; and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and saw that the face of the ground was drying.

NRSVCE.16: “Go out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

MSG.4: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ship landed on the Ararat mountain range.
MSG.5: The water kept going down until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains came into view.

NET.1: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and domestic animals that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth and the waters receded.

NET.3: The waters kept receding steadily from the earth, so that they had gone down by the end of the 150 days.
